name: silo-plugin-strapi-import
description: Import a Strapi 5 SQLite export into silo collections, from a panel in the admin

required.reason: To create one collection per Strapi list — the plan names each of them before anything is written.
To tell an existing collection from a name that is free, so the plan can warn you instead of failing halfway.
To write one entry per row. This is the import.

optional.reason: To put Strapi's uploads into silo's media library, so an imported entry points at a file silo holds rather than at your old Strapi. Without this, media fields keep their Strapi URL.
To recognise a file silo already holds, so re-importing does not upload every upload a second time and leave the first copy orphaned.
To count what is already in a target collection, and to support re-importing over it.
To empty a collection first, when you choose "replace" for it. Without this, replace is refused and append still works.

project.title: Target project
project.description: Where imported collections are created. The panel can override this per run.

collection_prefix.title: Collection name prefix
collection_prefix.description: Prepended to every proposed collection name, e.g. "strapi_". Empty means none.

media_base_url.title: Strapi media base URL
media_base_url.description: The Strapi instance the uploads are still served from, e.g. https://cms.example.com. Used for a file whose bytes you did not supply: it keeps this URL instead of importing, which silo resolves by leaving it alone. Empty leaves the paths relative.

media_folder.title: Media library folder
media_folder.description: Where supplied uploads land in silo's media library. Keeps a few hundred hashed Strapi filenames out of the library root. Empty means the root.

work_dir.title: Staging directory
work_dir.description: Where the uploaded .db and any supplied uploads are written while they are being read. Defaults to a silo-strapi-import directory under the system temp dir.

version.title: Which document version to read
version.description: Strapi 5 keeps a separate copy of every component row per draft and published version, so reading the tables directly would import each row twice.
